extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors preparing and submitting preprints to arXiv (registered authors of research articles)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and policy rules for preparing and submitting a research article (preprint) to arXiv, covering allowed file formats, figure handling, metadata, licensing, submission/announcement timing, and procedural responsibilities. Targeted at authors who will upload and manage their own arXiv submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered authors only
rubrics_metrics.description: We accept submissions only from registered authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only users who have registered accounts may submit articles. Ensure you have an arXiv account before attempting to submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: License to distribute / licensing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitters must grant arXiv.org a non-exclusive and irrevocable license to distribute or certify that the work is available under another license that conveys these rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must either grant arXiv the stated license or confirm an alternative license that provides the same distribution rights. This is a mandatory part of submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted text formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Your submission to the archive must be in one of the following formats (listed in order of preference): (La)TeX, AMS(La)TeX, PDFLaTeX; PDF; PostScript; HTML with JPEG/PNG/GIF images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: arXiv prefers TeX/LaTeX because it is open and preserves information. Note that arXiv will not accept dvi, PS, or PDF that were created from TeX/LaTeX source (submit the source instead). Users of word processors (e.g., Microsoft Word) should save as PDF. Scanned documents are not accepted, regardless of format.

rubrics_metrics.name: No omitted figures/tables/sections or abstract-only submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not accept submissions with omitted figures, tables or sections. We also do not accept 'abstract only' submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All substantive content intended to be part of the paper must be included in the submission; linking to figures on other servers is not an acceptable substitute. Abstract-only or deliberately incomplete submissions are disallowed because they are unhelpful and have limited archival value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formats for figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures can be in several common formats: PostScript (PS/EPS) for line drawings/plots; JPEG for photographic images; GIF or PNG for non-photographic images/bitmaps; PDF figures only with PDFLaTeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the format best matching the figure type (EPS/PS for vector/plots, JPEG for photos, PNG/GIF for bitmaps). If including figures with LaTeX source, use standard macro packages so they appear correctly (e.g., graphics, graphicx). PDF figures are only accepted when using PDFLaTeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure file size and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: If figure files are too large, readers with poor network connections will not be able to download them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make every effort to reduce figure size so papers remain accessible to users with limited bandwidth. See arXiv information on submission sizes and bitmapping help. If you have problems with a large submission, contact arXiv administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: No external-hosted omitted figures allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not accept submissions with omitted figures, even if you provide a link to another server.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All figures referenced in the paper must be included in the submission archive itself; external links do not substitute for included files.

rubrics_metrics.name: File name character restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv will accept only the following characters in file names: a-z A-Z 0-9 _ + - . , =
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any other characters (e.g., spaces, question marks, asterisks) will cause the system to reject the file upload or the submission. Use only the permitted characters to ensure portability and archival safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: File name and extension case sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: File names and extensions are case sensitive on our system; Figure1.PDF and figure1.pdf are not the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure internal file references (e.g., LaTeX figure inclusion commands) match the exact case of file names. Whether your local system is case sensitive or not, arXiv's storage is case sensitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of data sets and ancillary files is limited
rubrics_metrics.description: There are limited facilities for including data sets and ancillary files (data, programs, etc.) which are associated with articles submitted to arXiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the separate instructions about including data sets and ancillary files; do not assume arbitrary supplementary files will be accepted or hosted indefinitely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title/Abstract metadata preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate instructions exist on the preparation of separate title/abstract information used on the abstract pages, in announcements, in RSS feeds, and to support searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare title and abstract metadata according to the separate arXiv instructions so that announcements, feeds, and search indexing are correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check submission and read messages before final submit
rubrics_metrics.description: Before you make the final 'Submit Article' step be sure to check carefully both the title/abstract (metadata) and the processed files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you see errors or are unhappy with formatting, correct them before final submission or contact arXiv administrators if you cannot resolve problems. Carefully read system messages during processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsubmit option for corrections before announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: If you discover an error after submission but before public announcement then select the Unsubmit icon next to the submission on your user page to return it to the incomplete status allowing modification and later resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsubmitting removes the article from the processing queue; the announcement will be scheduled based on the later resubmission time. Use Unsubmit (not a new submission) to correct pre-announcement errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edits before announcement vs. versioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Edits before an article is publicly announced will not generate additional versions. The date stamp associated with the submission will be the time that the final 'Submit Article' step is completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make edits and finalize prior to announcement if you want a single announced version. Edits and final submission before 14:00 US Eastern Time Monday through Friday will not delay announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace original submission for corrections/errata (do not resubmit)
rubrics_metrics.description: DO NOT make a new submission for a corrected article or for an erratum. Rather replace the original submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the replace/edit workflow to update an existing arXiv record rather than creating a new, separate submission for minor corrections or errata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors must take responsibility / avoid third-party submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Because putting articles on arXiv entails certain responsibilities, authors must make their own submissions. Third-party submissions (by secretaries for example) are often the ones that cause the most problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the paper yourself to avoid errors arising from proxy submissions. Ensure you know and confirm the metadata and files during submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional affiliation required
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional affiliation for the author(s) must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accurate institutional affiliation information as part of the submission metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official report number(s) required
rubrics_metrics.description: Official report number(s) from the author(s) institution(s) must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your institution assigns report numbers, include them in the submission metadata where requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of submissions and announcement order / schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions to arXiv are normally made public on Sunday through Thursday, with no announcements Friday or Saturday. (Policy change 2017-01 regarding announcement order and the effect of edits.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Announcements follow a daily schedule tied to Eastern US times (table provided). Check the current time at the arXiv main site and the amount of time remaining before the daily 'freeze' to know when your submission will be announced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standard LaTeX packages for figure inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit figures with your (La)TeX source, use standard macro packages (e.g., the graphics and graphicx packages) so that the figures will appear in the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid nonstandard macros for figure inclusion. Note that arXiv administration cannot provide help with TeX-related issues, so seek help from colleagues if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact administrators for unresolved large-submission issues
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have problems with a large submission, contact arXiv administrators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For size or processing problems that you cannot resolve via the help pages, reach out to arXiv support; do not attempt workarounds that break the submission rules (e.g., omitting figures).
